clue.text: A jolly group on the sleeve

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the thing worn there

parts.note: a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
a band is a group, of musicians for instance

explanation.surface: Some cheerful crowd has been stitched onto a uniform sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective describing the group, but it is the old naval nickname for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of cloth is worn round the upper arm, over the sleeve, as a badge of mourning or office.

clue.text: Mixed bag-real letters for numbers in school

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A jumble of letters in a bag, with real letters standing for numbers in a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges the letters of BAG-REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The school subject uses symbols such as x and y in place of unknown numerical values.

clue.text: Output of a criminal potter — one guilty of professional misconduct

indicators.note: the output of a craftsman is what he makes from raw material, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Pottery made by a crook is the work of a dishonest professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Output of' rearranges the letters of A CRIMINAL POTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor or lawyer guilty of negligence or wrongdoing in practice is said to commit malpractice.

clue.text: Great man in short having a bitter before ten

indicators.note: before places the beer ahead of the ten

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer, an ale
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A famous man drinks a pint of bitter before ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale. The 'great man' is Alexander the Great, here in shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great's name shortened gives this familiar form.

clue.text: Air-beds blown up-arresting officers commonly use them

indicators.note: blown up suggests exploding, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Inflatable mattresses get pumped up before police officers make an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' looks like inflating air-beds, but it rearranges AIR-BEDS. 'Commonly' marks old slang.
explanation.definitionFit: This is old slang for handcuffs, which police officers put on people they arrest.

clue.text: eg Derby form, 100-1 put about

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: put about is a sailing phrase for turning round, so the Roman numerals are read backwards

parts.note: Roman numerals C for 100 and I for 1

explanation.surface: A racing tipster notes a horse's form at long odds of a hundred to one before the Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: '100-1' reads as betting odds, but it is the Roman numerals C and I, turned by 'put about' to give IC. The Derby is a famous English flat horse race at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the five English flat races called the Classics.

clue.text: Sloops for tailors

definitions.meaning: people in a clothing trade who shape fabric with shears

explanation.surface: Small boats are made for clothing makers.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fast sailing vessel is a type of sloop, and those who shape cloth in tailoring are so named.

clue.text: A duck-egg blue

parts.note: a duck in cricket and an egg (the shape of a zero) both mean nothing, nil

explanation.surface: A pale greenish-blue colour named after a duck's egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck-egg blue' reads as a paint colour, but duck and egg both mean zero. A duck in cricket is a score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigo shrub gives a dark dye, so its name stands for that shade of blue.

clue.text: Among them, idleness; envy sad in a way!

definitions.text: Among them, idleness; envy sad in a way!

parts.words: Among them, idleness; envy sad in a way!
parts.note: a list of vices including laziness and envy, which are grievous in a moral sense

explanation.surface: A list of failings including laziness and jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad in a way' means these vices are grave, deadly in the moral sense; idleness is sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian teaching lists pride, greed, lust, envy, gluttony, wrath and sloth as the gravest vices.

clue.text: White gown first worn in church in mixed choir's opening motet

definitions.text: White gown first worn in church

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are shuffled together

parts.note: the letters of the word with its S kept

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: At a church service, the choir begins with a motet while a baby wears a white gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges CHOIRS, keeping the S of the possessive, and 'opening motet' adds M.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrisom is the white robe put on a baby at baptism, its first church garment.

clue.text: Jason the dog?

parts.note: Jason of Greek myth fetched back the fleece of gold, so he is pictured as a dog breed that fetches

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Jason is the name of the family pet.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Jason and the Argonauts brought back the Golden Fleece, so he was literally a fetcher of the golden thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue reads the dog breed's name as a description of the mythical hero who brought back the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Dull retirement for Shakespeare

indicators.note: retirement suggests drawing back, so the word for dull is read backwards

parts.note: drab means dull or colourless

explanation.surface: Retiring to the country proved dreary for the great playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare is often called the Bard of Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, and Shakespeare is known simply as the Bard.

clue.text: Beekeeper's winter abroad

definitions.meaning: one who puts bees into a hive
the French word for the cold season, so 'abroad' points to a foreign language

explanation.surface: A beekeeper spends the cold months overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: One who hives bees is a hiver, and the French name for the coldest season is spelt the same way.

clue.text: Burden — and where it appears always to rest

definitions.text: where it appears always to rest
definitions.meaning: read as two words, the place where a burden seems always to fall is upon ourselves

explanation.surface: A weary complaint that the load always seems to land in the same place.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is a duty, and split into two words the answer says it always lands upon ourselves.

clue.text: Orderly over hospital in Welsh town

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first part on top of the second

parts.note: neat means tidy or orderly
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly works in a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital attendant, but it is an adjective meaning tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a town in south Wales.

clue.text: Tin and wooden vessel created by Lewis Carroll

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Noah's ark was a wooden boat

explanation.surface: A tin boat and a wooden boat both invented by the author of Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll wrote the poem The Hunting of the Snark.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary beast hunted in Carroll's nonsense poem is this creature, which he invented.

clue.text: Country folk, we hear

parts.note: rural people whose story is heard on the radio

explanation.surface: Gossip about people in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera, billed as 'an everyday story of country folk', so these country folk are heard, not seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio serial's family of farmers are the most famous country folk heard on British airwaves.

clue.text: Long shaft, pleasantly lit?

parts.note: a long ray of light from the sky, which makes things look pleasant

explanation.surface: A description of a long mine shaft or corridor with agreeable lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaft' suggests a mine or tunnel, but here it is a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of light from the sun is a long thin shaft that lights things warmly.

clue.text: Composer sounding at home in the UK?

indicators.note: sounding says the word for the country is said aloud to give a similar-sounding name

parts.note: the United Kingdom, Great Britain

explanation.surface: A musician who sounds very much at home in his own country.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten was a 20th-century English composer; his name is said like the name of his country.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten wrote the opera Peter Grimes and the War Requiem.

clue.text: Dollar butter cloth-that is very stiff

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: Money, butter and cloth seem to be on a shopping list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but 'one who butts', a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a coarse fabric stiffened with glue, used in bookbinding and hat-making.

clue.text: Five hundred sit about in fitful sun-they get tanned all over

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the rearranged word
fitful means irregular, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: about means the letters of the word are shuffled around

explanation.surface: Hundreds of people sit around under patchy sunshine to tan.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals work here: 'about' gives IST and 'fitful' gives NUS, and 'in' sets D with IST inside. 'Tanned all over' is the joke: no strap marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists sunbathe with no clothes, so they tan without strap marks.

clue.text: Laughs at some of the thunder I despise

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a thunderstorm they dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Laughs' lacked 'at': the answer is a transitive verb, so 'Laughs at' is the definition, and 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or ridicule someone is to laugh at them.

clue.text: Exiles king in storehouses

indicators.note: in means the king's letter goes inside the storehouses

parts.note: depots are warehouses or storehouses
R stands for king, from the Latin rex

explanation.surface: A king banishes people to warehouses.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb: to expel someone from a country is to banish or exile them.

clue.text: Having this, one can turn nuts!

definitions.text: Having this, one can turn nuts!

parts.words: Having this, one can turn nuts!
parts.note: a tool that grips and turns the metal fastenings, read as something that drives people mad

explanation.surface: Something that can make a person go crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn nuts' looks like going mad, but nuts here are the metal fastenings on bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: This hand tool grips a metal fastener so it can be twisted on or off a bolt.

clue.text: Charity-openers fashionable leading feature

parts.note: the opening letters of the word Charity
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A trendy charity launch is the main attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openers' is plural, so take the first two letters of 'Charity'. The chin leads because it juts out at the front of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaw's front point juts forward from the face, so it leads the other features.

clue.text: Skilful in cutting down a department

indicators.note: cutting down says the word department is shortened to its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Being good at trimming a department's budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting down' shortens DEPARTMENT to its standard abbreviation DEPT; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is skilful, as in being adept at something.

clue.text: Pitman said to be good talker in cage

indicators.note: said tells you the word for a coal worker is spoken aloud

parts.note: a pitman works in a coal pit, a miner

explanation.surface: A coal worker is said to chat well while in the lift cage at the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cage' sounds like the lift that carries miners down a shaft, but it is a bird cage.
explanation.definitionFit: This Asian starling is a caged bird famous for mimicking human speech.

clue.text: They sound like a ship's company — they are good sailors

indicators.note: sound like means the word for a ship's people is spoken aloud

parts.note: the people working on a ship are its crew

explanation.surface: Sailors described as both a ship's company and fine seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kroo (or Kru) are a West African people famous as seamen on European ships.
explanation.definitionFit: This Liberian people were long employed as skilled seamen on trading ships along the West African coast.

clue.text: Organ-effect from the choir

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sound in church comes from the singers.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'thE CHOir'.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ has a soft distant-sounding stop, the echo organ, giving a repeated-sound effect.

clue.text: Protection for tenant holding back a tear?

definitions.meaning: a legal cap on what a landlord may charge
a rip is a rent, and holding it back is restricting it

explanation.surface: Something that protects a tenant also stops someone crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal limits on what landlords charge protect tenants, and a tear in cloth is a rent, so limiting it is restricting a rent.

clue.text: Colours of deserts

definitions.meaning: abandons someone in a lonely place, as a verb

explanation.surface: The shades of the sandy wastelands.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownish-crimson shades bear this name, and to strand someone on an island is to abandon or desert them.

clue.text: Last of silver spoons put out for godparent

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of the word are rearranged
Last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The traditional christening present of silver spoons is laid out by a godparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' rearranges SPOONS to SPONSO, and 'Last of silver' adds R at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor at a baptism makes promises on the child's behalf, as a godparent does.
